headline: Gas shortage forces closure of essential commodity factories across Bangladesh, impacting supply chains
summary: Major industrial groups, including MGI and TK Group, have halted production of vital goods like edible oil, flour, and sugar due to severe gas supply disruptions, raising concerns about market availability.
details: Meghna Group of Industries (MGI) in Narayanganj has shut down 12 essential commodity processing factories, including those for soybean oil, flour, and other daily necessities, due to a severe gas crisis. Production had been declining for days before the complete halt on Wednesday.

MGI is a significant player in the essential goods market, accounting for 22% of the country's total imports of seven key products and raw materials last fiscal year. Their factories process approximately 9,000 tons of goods daily, totaling around 3.3 million tons annually.

The gas crisis extends beyond MGI, with several other major essential commodity processors also halting production or operating significantly below capacity. Some are attempting to use alternative fuels to maintain limited operations.

The crisis intensified after one of the two floating LNG terminals in Maheshkhali, Cox's Bazar, operated by Excelerate Energy, shut down on July 21 due to a fire and technical fault. This reduced the national grid's gas supply by approximately 450 million cubic feet daily.

Although the terminal partially resumed operations on August 6 and was at about half capacity by August 12, gas supply to the national grid dropped to 2.03 billion cubic feet on Wednesday. This created a deficit of about 1.77 billion cubic feet against a daily demand of approximately 3.85 billion cubic feet.

Industry leaders, including MGI Chairman Mostofa Kamal, are urging emergency gas supply to keep these factories operational and ensure the normal flow of essential goods. Businesses fear prolonged shortages will disrupt the supply of finished products, even with raw materials available.

The impact is not limited to essential commodities; gas and boiler-dependent industries like steel, glass, and textiles are also experiencing production disruptions. Petro Bangla and energy sector officials confirmed severe shortages in industrial and power sectors during the LNG terminal shutdown.

Other affected groups include TK Group, which has closed 20 out of 28 processing factories, and Smile Food Products, with three large factories shut down. Delta Agrofood and City Group are also facing significant production hurdles due to the gas shortage.

The government plans to import five more cargoes of LNG this month to address the ongoing supply crunch. This measure aims to alleviate the severe gas deficit affecting industrial production and the supply chain of essential goods.

headline: 53 Awami League activists arrested in Dhaka for 'banned' August 15 activities
summary: Police apprehended 53 Awami League and affiliate members from a preparatory meeting in Bhatara, Dhaka. Authorities claim they were planning 'flash processions' and 'violence' across the capital.
details: Fifty-three leaders and activists of the Awami League and its affiliated organizations were arrested by Bhatara police in Dhaka. They were apprehended from a preparatory meeting for August 15 activities, which are currently banned for the party.

The arrests took place on Thursday night (August 13) around 9 PM, from a building on Road 28 in Block M of Bashundhara Residential Area, Bhatara Thana. Officer-in-Charge Md. Mazharul Islam confirmed the arrests.

According to OC Mazharul Islam, the individuals were preparing to observe National Mourning Day on August 15 and also planned 'flash processions' in various parts of the capital. Police claim they intended to carry out violence in different locations across Dhaka.
Several placards and banners were recovered from their possession during the raid. Police stated that cases would be filed against all 53 arrested individuals under the Anti-Terrorism Act.
